subject: Raising Cane's Fellsway Plaza Proposal
overview: The development team for Raising Cane's presented plans for a new 3,326-square-foot restaurant at Fellsway Plaza, highlighting site design, traffic flow, and architectural standards. The meeting served as a public introduction ahead of formal filings for site plan review and a special permit.

items.title: Project Introduction and Overview
items.summary: Attorney Kathleen Desmond introduced the development team and outlined the proposal for a drive-through restaurant to be built in an underutilized section of Fellsway Plaza.

items.title: Company History and Operations
items.summary: Adam Caracci provided a history of the family-owned company, its 'focused' chicken finger menu, and its model for community marketing and crew retention.

items.title: Site Engineering and Pedestrian Connectivity
items.summary: Project engineer Eric DeBrule detailed the 31,000-square-foot lease area, noting that the plan increases total green space and improves sidewalk connections from Riverside Avenue and Fellsway.

items.title: Drive-Through Logistics
items.summary: The team explained their dual-lane drive-through system, which uses crew members with handheld tablets during peak hours to maximize efficiency and prevent vehicle queuing.

items.title: Architectural Design and Aesthetics
items.summary: Representatives presented interior and exterior renderings featuring a 'warehouse' feel with brick, metal, and glass materials tailored to the local community.

items.title: Traffic Impact and Access Management
items.summary: Traffic engineer Pat Dunford addressed neighborhood concerns regarding vehicle maneuverability and potential congestion, stating that consolidated curb cuts and a large queue capacity will mitigate impacts on Riverside Avenue.
